producer_report.summary: Added the reading replay, as planned. `athena check-reading --request <file> --reading <file>` prints `accept` or `refuse: <reason>` using `check_reading_acceptance`. Before the verifier, every job replays the newest 50 requests that have an accepted reading through the base and candidate builds. The result is stored as a new typed record, `athena.replay/1` at `<job>/replay.json`. More than 10% newly refused holds the job: `verify::apply_replay_hold` runs right after `judge()` and adds an Athena Blocker finding that names the list, so the job ends Rejected and is not landed. Exactly 10% or less is not held. The 10% is the code constant `REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT`, tested with integer maths. Criteria that state an intent to refuse more also stop the hold, and the replay is still recorded. An empty history, a tree without `athena-cli`, a failed build, a build without the subcommand, a nested run, or an unreadable answer gives `no replay: <reason>`. That is never a pass and never a partial count. The replay makes no model call and has no skip switch. Its build directory is removed before the pre-verifier disk check. The verifier brief gets a "Reading replay" section: count, total, at most 20 entries with reasons cut to 160 characters, and the whole section capped at 4096 bytes. Without a usable replay it shows `no replay: <reason>`. The test seam is a `#[cfg(test)]` thread-local pair of checkers, consulted before tree resolution and the subcommand probe. fmt, clippy with warnings denied, `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` and the full `cargo test --locked` all passed. The production path (building both trees and running `check-reading` on each) was not exercised by any test, because it needs a real two-tree build.

criteria_check.criterion: `athena check-reading` takes a stored request and reading and prints accept or refuse with the reason, using the same acceptance rules as reading.rs; a fixture test shows both outputs (cargo test -p athena-cli).
criteria_check.evidence: The new test `check_reading_prints_accept_or_refuse_with_the_reason_the_reading_rules_give` in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs passes (`cargo test -p athena-cli --bin athena check_reading`). It parses the clap subcommand, asserts `accept` for a clean fixture, and asserts a `refuse: ...` line carrying the reason for a criterion that rests on the producer's report. That line equals the one built from `check_reading_acceptance` called directly.

open_issues: The real production path is untested: building both trees, probing `check-reading --help`, and running the binary per reading. Only the checker seam, the comparison, the hold rule, the record, the finding and the brief are covered. The first live use will show whether the build environment from `athena_agent::env::build` (PATH, HOME, CARGO_HOME) is enough for `cargo build --locked -p athena-cli`.

Departure from the plan: the plan listed `replay_readings(records, base, candidate, criteria)`; the final signature takes inputs from `replay_inputs` plus the job id and the two commit ids, to keep selection and comparison separately testable. Replay tests live in a separate `replay_tests` module in reading.rs, and the shared fixtures in a `#[cfg(test)]` module `replay_fixtures`. The replay `Replay::none` constructor lives in athena-data records.rs.
Two files outside the brief's expected deliverables were changed, as the plan required: crates/athena-core/src/store.rs (the `job_of` arm and a load test) and docs/records.md (a layout row).
The replay checks the stored request and reading only, with no earlier attempt or referenced jobs, so rules that need earlier jobs (`check_prior_result_and_scope` for retries) pass trivially in it.
The intent phrase list (REFUSAL_RISE_INTENT) is a judgment call that maintainers may want to widen.

The replay builds both trees on every job in a repository that has `crates/athena-cli`. That is slow, and `elapsed_s` in the record shows the cost. The build directory is removed before the disk gate.
mistakes: I first named a helper `one_line` in briefs.rs, which clashed with an existing function. I renamed it `replay_one_line`.

The first draft of the production build function left a placeholder `leak_path` closure and an `unreachable!` stub. I replaced both with the real build and probe code before the first compile of the test build.
The first pipeline helper dropped the test repository directory on return, so reads of the repository failed. I now return the directories with the result.
I ran one command with a redirect that was denied. I reran it without the redirect.
learnings: `Records::load` panics (`expect("every other record names its job")`) for any AnyRecord variant that `store.rs::job_of` does not name, so every new job-level record kind needs a `job_of` arm.
`crate::checks::run_check` keeps only the last 4096 bytes of output, redacted. `check-reading` therefore caps its printed line at 3000 bytes so the `refuse:` prefix survives.

Existing pipeline test `a_fake_job_takes_its_baseline_before_the_producer_and_numbers_the_invocations_in_order` counts the progress lines of a run (6). The new `replay` line makes it 7, so that test was updated.
The fake pipeline runs `athena.go` on the test's own thread, so a thread-local test override works there.
`SnapshotRepo::None` gives a plain checkout of one commit, usable for a build.
Both trees share one CARGO_TARGET_DIR in the replay, so the first build's `athena` binary is copied out before the second build overwrites it.
desires: A way to exercise the real two-tree build and `check-reading` path in a test. The production path builds both trees with `cargo build` and runs `check-reading` on each, and no test runs it, because the pipeline tests use the test override.
